eps.t: All For A Couple Of Ponies

eps.d: When an overbearing young high-pressure business man receives death threats, Marker is put on as bodyguard. The arrogant executive is having an affair with an employee's wife, so the husband makes a move against him- but is he the only one?

"'And a Very Fine Fiddle Has He"

Protection Is a Man's Best Friend

eps.d: Runaways from the country are lured by the glamour of London, only to fall into the hands of recruiters for call girl rings. Jennie is one, and she soon becomes hard and cynical. Marker is hired to find her and coax her to return home.

eps.t: You Should Hear Me Eat Soup
You Have to Draw the Line Somewhere
All the Black Dresses She Wants

eps.d: Marker moves into new offices in Birmingham, and is engaged to track down a missing husband.

eps.t: I Could Set It to Music
It's a Terrible Way to Be
Works with Chess, Not with Life

eps.d: A librarian suspects that his wife posed for The Bromsgrove Venus, and asks Marker to find out whether she has been having an affair with the photographer.

eps.t: It Must be The Architecture - Can't be The Climate
eps.d: Marker investigates when a female patient dies under the care of a doctor with whom she had had a relationship.

eps.t: It's Learning about the Lies that Hurts
There's No Future in Monkey Business
Cross that Palm When We Come to It

eps.d: Released on Parole Frank finds it difficult back on the outside.
Marker gains employment on a building site and exposes a swindle by a rocker.
Frank is accused of stealing a colleagues wages.
Marker tries to save a fellow lodger who tries to kill herself.
Marker joins a local detective agency, and has to gather evidence to help a man accused of murdering a local garage owner.
Frank is instructed to find a stage-struck teenager who has run away from home.
Mrs. Mortimer's ex-husband calls and disrupts the routine of the household.
After Frank saves an old lady from a potential shoplifting charge, and recognises her financially desperate son as a former fellow prison inmate, he's contacted by the man's worried wife.

eps.t: Well-There was This Girl, You See...
eps.d: Things are looking up when Marker is invited to join an enquiry agency.
Marker is hired to find out who is making threatening phone calls to a woman living alone.

eps.t: I Always Wanted a Swimming Pool
eps.d: Things get unusual when Marker is hired to watch the antics of a wayward husband.
When Marker reluctantly agrees to try to find a woman's missing husband, but facts about the story he's been told by the woman don't add up, he enlists the help of Inspector Firbank.
Marker encounters some strong and powerful women.

eps.t: And When You've Paid the Bill, You're None the Wiser
eps.d: His latest case leads Marker into the centre of a family squabble.

eps.t: Who Wants to Be Told Bad News?
eps.d: Marker is hired to look after a client's welfare.

eps.t: The Man Who Didn't Eat Sweets
eps.d: Marker is hired after a lady finds a picture of a young woman in her husband's wallet.
It appears as though Marker's interests and those of D.I. Firbanks are the same - but are they?
Marker finds a case involving an old reprobate and a young American visiting Britain.
Marker takes on an investigation and finds himself manipulated by several people ̶ including DI Firbank.
Marker is faced with a head-on collision with D.I. Firbank.
Marker is hired to enquire into the activities of a bankrupt shirt manufacturer and uncovers a web of deceit.
Marker is hired to discover the whereabouts of a missing Janice Summers, and bring her back home.
A routine credit inquiry leads Marker to uncover some strange discoveries concerning an eminent doctor's wife.
Marker is hired to babysit Mrs. Podmore's pet cat, Bertie, but things have a way of turning awkward.
A man calls to ask Marker to find out whether his wife is having an affair, but ha has a hidden agenda.
A husband asks Marker to investigate his wife thinking she's having an affair, but is he having an affair aswell?
Marker is hired to establish why a housekeeper received a large bequest from her late employer.
Frank is hired to find a missing man.
Marker investigates the apparent theft of a new breed of rose.
Marker's ex-landlady asks him to investigate her son's new employer.
A woman asks Marker to find out whether her football-fanatic husband has been "playing away".
A church warden hires Marker to find out who is behind a series of "poison pen" letters accusing the new vicar of sexual impropriety.
Marker saves a hotel resident who has attempted suicide, then tries to find out why an apparently privileged young woman would want to die.
Marker tangles with some gangsters over a horse-doping racket.

eps.t: How About a Cup of Tea?
eps.d: Marker considers a change of career after his beating, but agrees to take on a case involving tenants who are in arrears.
Marker reluctantly decides to gets his own back on the people who attacked him. An ex-policeman has a business proposal.

eps.t: They All Sound Simple at First
eps.d: Marker, now working with Ron Gash in Walton, pursues a debt owed to a local craftsman by his brother-in-law.
A woman asks Marker to gather evidence of her husband's adultery.
A man hires Marker to trace his missing wife.
Marker moves into his new office and a troublesome first day.
An offer from a wealthy client is to much for Marker to refuse.
Marker searches for a young university student - and comes face to face with violence.
A middle-aged man engages Marker to trace his wife, whom he claims is living with another man, but he has lied and it is the man he is really interested in.
A concerned woman asks Marker to investigate her father, the chief clerk at an engineering firm.
Marker is engaged to track down a former council employee who has accepted bribes from a corrupt property developer.

Frank goes undercover at a hotel when the owner is convinced that her son's new wife is a gold digger. This is the very final episode of the series. At the time Alfred Burke told the TV Times that that was it but also said that was the case every season.
